question.text: In a 'Unified Structure', offshore and domestic capital are pooled at which level?

answer.text: At a Mauritius pooling vehicle only.
At a Singapore feeder fund only.
At the onshore Indian AIF (foreign investors route through automatic FDI into the Indian AIF).
Each investor invests directly in Indian investee companies.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 105), in a Unified Structure the domestic and offshore commitments are pooled into a single onshore SEBI-registered AIF. Where an offshore fund is used as a vehicle for foreign investors, the offshore fund invests in the onshore AIF through the automatic FDI route and is treated as one investor alongside the domestic investors in the Indian AIF. The Trap: Mauritius-only describes a pure-offshore design. Singapore-only describes a master-feeder design. Direct investment by each investor describes a parallel structure - not unified pooling. Note: Per page 106, when an offshore fund is interposed between foreign investors and the onshore AIF, both the offshore fund and the onshore AIF have their respective investment managers, who are paid management and performance fees at their respective levels.
